title: Powerful 7.7 magnitude earthquake rocks Panama
summary: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck southern Panama on Friday, damaging buildings and sending thousands into the streets, but the country appeared to escape widespread destruction or deaths.

blocks.text: World·New
A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck southern Panama on Friday, damaging buildings and sending thousands into the streets, but the country appeared to escape widespread destruction or deaths.
Country appears to have escaped widespread destruction or deaths
Powerful earthquake hits Panama, triggers tsunami warnings

The ‌U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) said the earthquake hit at a depth of 12.6 kilometres, with an epicentre in a sparsely populated area about 200 kilometres from the capital, and that some casualties were possible.

In the following hours, even as more than 40 aftershocks rattled the isthmus nation, the Panama Canal and Cobre Panama copper mine reported normal operations and the Tocumen International Airport lifted ​a suspension on flights.
Office workers in the upscale business hub of downtown Panama City ​fretted about how to get home in the snarl of traffic, after the quake sent thousands into the streets.
Juan Sanchez, a 37-year-old Economy Ministry employee, waited for a bus he said he doubted would arrive.

"They evacuated all of ​these buildings. Everyone is outside. Now the problem is, how do we get home?"
President Raul Mulino travelled to Penonome, ⁠a city about halfway between the epicentre ⁠and Panama City, where some buildings collapsed and a church was damaged.

blocks.text: Despite the ‌force of Friday's tremor, the country appeared to have been spared the destruction of other recent powerful quakes in the region, with no deaths or injuries immediately reported.
Back-to-back quakes in Venezuela in June killed several thousand people, while a quake in Colombia in August killed more than 300.
Cars are seen crushed under a collapsed building after an earthquake in Penonome, Panama, on Friday. (Martin Bernetti/AFP/Getty Images)

An exposure report by the USGS estimated about 43,000 Panamanians lived in areas with at least severe exposure ⁠to the quake. This compares with nearly 1.4 million in the area of the twin quakes in Venezuela and over 1.6 million in the quake-hit zone of western Colombia.
Nestor Luque, director of Panama's geosciences institute, attributed the quake to the Azuero Sona Fault System that he said contained a massive buildup of pressure ‌that is occasionally released.
"The seismic signals have travelled throughout the national territory and that is why it could be felt everywhere."
People gather on a street in Panama City after an earthquake on Friday. (Enea Lebrun/Reuters)
In Panama City, Luque said he counted 40 seconds of vibrations, though other areas may have felt even longer tremors.
Sabina Rios, who was on the sixth floor of an old U.S. military-era building in Panama City, said the shaking was unusually strong and prolonged.
"The quake felt strong ​and lasted a long time, the longest I've felt in years," Rios said.
People look at a damaged government building in Penonome on Friday. (Martin Bernetti/AFP/Getty Images)

Victor Pinzon, a 48-year-old maintenance worker, told Reuters he had watched high-rise window cleaners ride out the shaking. "It's a miracle they didn't ⁠get killed," he said. "They looked like they were swinging in a hammock."
Strong earthquakes are not common in Panama, and some elderly residents were in ⁠tears as they evacuated into the streets.

"We're scared. It's just the two of us old folks here. The house has cracked, and we're afraid ⁠it ⁠could fall on us," said Ricardo Brown, 74, in Herrera ​province in southern Panama, where he said he saw a number of damaged homes.
A statue is seen by the earthquake in Penonome on Friday. (Martin Bernetti/AFP/Getty Images)

Omar Smith, who heads Panama's civil protection agency, told news outlet Telemetro Reporta ​that impacts had also been reported in Chitre, ⁠the capital of Herrera, and along the coast in Los Santos province.
The USGS estimated economic losses could amount to 1 to 10 per cent of Panama's gross domestic product, and electricity provider Naturgy reported power outages in six provinces.
Panama was due to hold a national evacuation drill on Monday of next week to test the country's emergency response.
